jobs.excerpt: Zipliens is a leading lien resolution company that specializes in streamlining the lien resolution process for personal injury law firms.
jobs.description:
Zipliens is a leading lien resolution company that specializes in streamlining the lien resolution process for personal injury law firms. We are looking for proactive, results-driven individuals to join our dynamic team.

We are seeking a VP of Customer Support to build Zipliens' support function from the ground up. Reporting to the Chief Customer Officer and sitting within the Customer Experience department alongside the VP of Customer Success, this role owns inbound, reactive support for the firms that use Zipliens, along with the operating foundation that makes that support consistent, measurable, and able to scale.

Owning Customer Support at Zipliens is a greenfield opportunity. HubSpot is our core platform for the foreseeable future, and you will design and configure omnichannel support within it, integrating other channels and tools as needed. You will start as a hands-on individual contributor: setting the vision and strategy, configuring the systems, defining reporting standards, and proposing the team and organization build-out as volume and complexity warrant.

Our primary customers are law firm users. Over time, you will also help design a client support experience for claimants that strengthens our value to the firms we serve and helps them deliver better outcomes for their own clients, where that support is desired. You will partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Engineering, Lien Resolution Operations, Finance, Sales, and Marketing.

In your first year, you will focus on:

  • Defining the support strategy and operating model: tiers, scope, channels, hours of coverage, and what Support does and does not own, including triage-level services questions.
  • Standing up omnichannel intake in HubSpot, starting with form submissions, adding chat as an option, integrating phone into the same system, and recommending whether and when to add social channels.
  • Establishing Tier 3 service levels with Engineering and Product, including severity definitions, handoff criteria, and a shared escalation process.
  • Setting reporting standards and a baseline for first response, resolution time, backlog, customer satisfaction, contact reasons, and cost to serve.
  • Building an AI-forward support model that combines a knowledge base, self-service, deflection, triage, and agent assist, with human review where accuracy matters.
  • Proposing the team and organization build-out, including roles, hiring sequence, and capacity model tied to volume data.
  • Evaluating an enterprise or white-glove support tier using cost-to-serve and segmentation data and market research, and bringing a recommendation to the relevant executives.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Support Strategy & Function Leadership

  • Function Ownership: Own the support vision, strategy, and outcomes, translating company priorities into support goals and an operating plan.
  • Hands-On Execution: Work the queue and configure systems directly in the first phase while the function is being built, and move to leading through others as the team is approved and hired.
  • Org Design & Capacity Planning: Propose the team structure, role definitions, hiring sequence, and capacity model, and build a team with clear career paths once approved.
  • Operating Cadence: Run a regular rhythm of metrics reviews and reporting to the CCO and executive team.

Omnichannel Operations & Systems

  • Data Integration & Tooling: Define requirements and establish data flows (such as syncing portal data, case status, CSM data, and customer context) to ensure support agents have seamless visibility into customer history and operational data.
  • HubSpot Ownership: Own the configuration and reporting of support in HubSpot, including ticketing, routing, deflection, service levels, utilization of the knowledge base, and automation, so the data is trustworthy enough to make decisions on.
  • Channel Strategy: Define how customers reach Support across form submissions, chat, phone, and social, and sequence the rollout of each channel.
  • Voice Support: Integrate phone into HubSpot and define coverage, voicemail handling, and staffing so that no call or message depends on a single person.
  • Documentation: Create and maintain support playbooks, SOPs, macros, and internal help content as living assets with named owners and a review cadence; partner with Enablement on knowledge base content and strategy.

Service Levels, Escalation & Quality

  • Tiering & Triage: Own Tier 1/1.5/2 technical support and define what is resolved in Support, what is routed elsewhere, and what triage-level services support looks like for now.
  • Tier 3 Service Levels: Agree on response and resolution targets with Engineering and Product for Tier 3 issues.
  • Quality Standards: Set quality, coaching, and customer satisfaction standards for the function and report against them.
  • Incident Communication: Partner with Product and Engineering on customer communication during incidents and known issues.

Customer Experience & Insight

  • Firm Users: Design the support experience around firm users, who are our primary customers.
  • Claimant Experience: Help define a client support experience for claimants that supports firms in delivering better client outcomes, for firms that choose it.
  • Enterprise Support Model: Use cost-to-serve, segmentation data, and market research to propose and develop an enterprise or white-glove service level with the CFO, CEO, and CCO.
  • Voice of Customer Input: Provide contact-reason data and support trends to the Voice of Customer program and to Product prioritization.

AI & Automation

  • AI-Forward Support Model: Identify and implement where AI improves resolution time, consistency, and cost to serve, such as triage, deflection, knowledge base creation, and agent assist, and define where human review is required.
  • Measurement: Track the effect of automation on quality, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve, and adjust accordingly.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Customer Success: Partner with the VP of Customer Success as well as Lien Resolution Operations to ensure customers move between Support, ops, and account management without repeating themselves.
  • Product & Engineering: Partner on bug triage, Tier 3 service levels, release readiness, and defect trends.
  • Lien Resolution Operations: Partner on routing services questions and aligning customer-facing commitments with operational execution.
  • Finance: Partner on cost-to-serve analysis, headcount modeling, and the business case for any new service level.
  • Sales & Marketing: Partner on help center content, release communication, and customer-facing materials.
  • Integration Partners: Partner with our integration partners on API support and on service level commitments for mutual customers, including how issues are triaged and handed off when they span both platforms.

Qualifications:

  • 7+ years in customer support, technical support, or support operations within B2B SaaS or tech-enabled services, including 3+ years in a leadership role.
  • Experience building or materially rebuilding a support function, including tiers, service levels, routing, knowledge base, quality assurance, and reporting.
  • Hands-on experience configuring a support platform. HubSpot experience is strongly preferred; experience with comparable tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, or Salesforce Service Cloud is acceptable.
  • Experience implementing omnichannel intake, including integrating phone and chat with a ticketing system.
  • Comfort operating as both an individual contributor and a leader: able to work the queue and configure systems while designing the organization.
  • Experience defining and reporting support metrics such as first response, resolution time, backlog, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve.
  • Experience aligning on escalation service levels with engineering or product teams.
  • Practical experience applying AI in support, such as triage, deflection, knowledge generation, or agent assist.
  • Strong analytical and written communication skills, including the ability to build a business case and present it to executives.
  • Experience in legal services, personal injury, litigation-adjacent technology, or a related professional services industry is preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree required. Focus in business, law, or a related field is preferred.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%, primarily for company offsites and support industry events.

Benefits

  • Private Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Company HSA contributions for HDHP participants
  • Flexible Spending Accounts (Health & Dependent Care)
  • Company-Paid Short-Term Disability Coverage
  • Voluntary Long-Term Disability, Life, AD&D, and Supplemental Coverage Options
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick Time & Select Holidays)
  • Paid Parental Leave

Pay Disclosure: The total base salary range for this role is $179,500 - $243,000 annually, with the opportunity for a discretionary bonus. Final compensation will be determined based on skills and experience.

jobs.excerpt: Development Specialist WashingtonThe OpportunityPlease consider joining our team!
jobs.description:
Development Specialist
Washington

The Opportunity

Please consider joining our team! Reach Out and Read Northwest, an affiliate of the national Reach Out and Read program, reaches 200,000 families annually across Washington and Oregon, distributing over 330,000 books through 3,200 medical providers in over 400 clinics. Our focus is on serving underserved communities, where 62% of the children we reach are from low-income families, 42% identify as children of color, and 21% speak a home language other than English. Together, we contribute to the broader impact of the organization, which serves 4.6 million children across the country and distributes over 7.7 million books annually.

The Development Specialist is an early-career fundraising professional who brings strong writing and editing skills and thrives on collaboration. After an initial onboarding period, they will take on a significant share of our grant writing, drafting proposals and reports for review by the Associate Director of Development, while keeping deadlines on track, maintaining Salesforce data, and ensuring funders are thanked and stewarded well.

The Development Specialist reports to the Associate Director of Development and works closely with program team members coordinates with Regional Executive Director serving as an integrator who helps teams share information and meet funder commitments. As the Development Specialist grows in the role, they will have opportunities to take on more of the grant cycle, build relationships with funders, and develop their own portfolio over time.

Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Grant Writing and Reporting (50%)

  • Work alongside the Associate Director of Development to learn our programs, funders, and proposal library, then grow into drafting the majority of foundation and corporate proposals and reports

  • Write and edit grant proposals, adapting existing templates and boilerplate and translating program impact into clear, compelling, funder-aligned narratives

  • Coordinate the grant reporting process: gather program and financial information from colleagues, prepare drafts, and ensure interim and final reports are submitted accurately and on time

  • Maintain and update proposal templates, boilerplate language, and resource documents, including visually engaging materials created in Canva or similar tools

  • Support prospect research and funder qualification as requested

Grant Project Management and Collaboration (30%)

  • Manage the Northwest grants calendar, planning weeks ahead so applications, deliverables, and reports are on track well before deadlines

  • Track grant requirements, deliverables, and timelines in Asana, keeping teams informed and following up with the right colleagues for content and approvals

  • Help prepare agendas and materials for biweekly development team meetings

  • Enter and maintain grant and donor data in Salesforce, ensuring accuracy and alignment with National standards

  • Run recurring Salesforce reports, such as monthly or quarterly pipeline and grant status reports, to support team planning

  • Clearly communicate grant requirements and restrictions to leadership and finance, and submit backup materials promptly

Donor Stewardship and Acknowledgement (20%)

  • Facilitate donor and funder acknowledgment, ensuring gifts and grants are thanked promptly and personally

  • Prepare materials and briefings for stewardship and cultivation meetings led by the Associate Director of Development and Executive Director, and join select funder meetings to learn and inform upcoming proposals

  • Draft follow-up applications and communications that result from these opportunities

  • Support additional development projects as requested

Qualifications and Experience

There are innumerable ways to learn, grow, and excel professionally. We respect this commitment to growth when we review applications and take a broad look at the experience of each applicant. We want to get to know you and the unique strengths you will bring to the work. We will honor your lived and professional experience as key aspects of your candidacy for the role and prioritize applicants with experience dismantling the structural inequities that disproportionately impact children and families with traditionally marginalized identities.

  • Commitment to equity in opportunities and outcomes for children, with recognition of factors including race, ethnicity, language, and socioeconomic status

  • Approximately two to three years of experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, or a related role where writing was a regular part of the work

  • Project management skills: you can juggle multiple deadlines, plan ahead, keep a calendar on track, and follow through on details

  • Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with the ability to turn information from many sources into clear, compelling narratives and produce solid first drafts on a steady timeline

  • A collaborative approach and a track record of working effectively across teams, building trust with colleagues, and keeping people informed

  • Comfort working with data and an appreciation for why accurate, up-to-date records matter

  • Self-motivation and the ability to work independently in a remote environment while staying connected to the team

  • Experience supporting grant proposals, reports, compliance, or donor stewardship, even if you did not lead them (preferred)

  • Experience with Salesforce or another donor database, including running reports (preferred)

  • Familiarity with Asana, Canva, and similar project management and design tools (preferred)

Compensation, Benefits & Position Details

This is a full-time, non-exempt position, consistent with how Reach Out and Read Northwest classifies other professional roles in Washington State and reflective of the state's salary threshold requirements. The annualized equivalent compensation range is $70,000 to $75,000, commensurate with experience. Employees in this classification are eligible for overtime pay in accordance with Washington State law. ROR offers a robust benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan with match, paid time off, and more. The role is fully remote and requires candidates to be based in Washington State. This role requires occasional local travel and three to five overnight trips per year (less than 5% of the time)

How to Apply

Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications through our online portal. The interview process will include a preliminary screening, followed by a hiring manager interview with the Associate Director of Development. Advancing candidates will participate in a virtual final interview with other members of the Reach Out and Read team, as well as an in-person meet-and-greet with the Associate Director of Development.

Commitment to Diversity

Reach Out and Read is committed to building an organization that embraces diversity, pursues equity, and fosters an environment of inclusion. ROR sits at the intersection of health and education, uniquely positioned to play a critical role in addressing systemic disparities and inequities in the public health framework. ROR strives to be an antiracist organization, using its influence to fight against social injustice by supporting a culture of learning, empowerment, equity, and a deep appreciation for the unique experiences that we each bring to our communities. And we believe that changing the world begins with holding ourselves and our workplace to that same standard.

About Reach Out and Read

Founded in 1989, Reach Out and Read is a national nonprofit organization working to ensure that all families have the opportunity to create meaningful everyday moments through shared reading aloud and relationship-building. By leveraging pediatric care to champion the positive effects of reading daily and distributing books, Reach Out and Read gives young children a foundation for success and reaches 4.6 million children across the country – half of whom identify as BIPOC and two-thirds of whom come from low-income families.

Reach Out and Read's tens of thousands of trained pediatric providers use books as a diagnostic tool during regular check-ups and teach parents how to engage their child with a book to promote positive parent-child interactions during the rapid brain growth between birth and age five. The daily practice of reading aloud with a parent supports children's literacy and math skill development, their social-emotional development, and prepares them for future success in school. Working together with our sites and providers, we leverage our three decades of expertise, build on our literacy foundations, and engage our shared networks as a catalyst for change, focusing on equitably strengthening and deepening our impact on the children, families, and communities we serve.

The Impact:

  • Reach Out and Read program sites are located in 6,500 clinics, safety net hospitals, medical systems, and other healthcare settings in all 50 states and the District of Columbia.

  • Reach Out and Read serves 4.6 million children and their families annually.

  • More than 7.7 million new, developmentally appropriate books are integrated into well-child visits with families annually.

  • 39,000 clinicians currently participate in Reach Out and Read.

  • Our peer-reviewed body of evidence demonstrates that Reach Out and Read parents are two-and-a-half times more likely to read regularly to their children, and that children experiencing Reach Out and Read show enhanced language development.

To learn more about Reach Out and Read,.

ROR is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Reach Out and Read is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, cultural heritage, ancestry, political belief, age, marital status, pregnancy, physical or mental disability, or veteran status. Reach Out and Read is compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act and we are committed to making special accommodations for your interview or work as a member of our team. Position: Vollzeit (40h)

Du willst dafür sorgen, dass unsere Theken in hunderten Drogeriefilialen so aussehen, wie wir sie geplant haben: vollständig, intakt und aktuell bestückt?

Dann bist du bei uns richtig. Unser Handelsgeschäft wächst, und du gestaltest mit, wie unser Auftritt in der Filiale mitwächst.

Das sind wir!

Maniko ist ein innovatives, schnell wachsendes Unternehmen in der Nagelkosmetik-Branche, das hochwertige Produkte für anspruchsvolle Kundinnen europaweit anbietet. Wir sind bekannt für unsere selbstklebende UV Gel Nail Strips-Technologie, die professionelle Ergebnisse bequem von zu Hause aus ermöglicht – und haben mit unseren Soft Gel Press-On Nails eine zweite starke Produktlinie im Markt.

Unsere Produkte stehen national bei dm, dm Österreich, Rossmann und budni im Regal, und unser Handelsgeschäft wächst weiter. Aus dem Startup ist ein Unternehmen geworden, das im Regal mit den großen Beauty-Marken konkurriert. Groß genug, dass deine Arbeit in tausenden Filialen sichtbar wird, und beweglich genug, dass du Strukturen noch selbst baust, statt sie zu verwalten.

Unser Geheimnis? Ein leidenschaftliches Team, das sich nicht mit dem Status quo zufrieden gibt und ständig danach strebt, besser zu werden. Wir glauben an Werte, die wirklich gelebt werden – keine leeren Phrasen. Bei uns heißt es:

  • Facts over Ego: Daten und Ergebnisse stehen über allem – bei uns zählt das Beste für das Team und das Unternehmen, nicht das persönliche Ego.

  • Challenge accepted: Wir sehen in jeder Herausforderung eine Chance, an der wir wachsen können.

  • Power to the people: Vertrauen und Verantwortung gehen bei uns Hand in Hand – dein Impact zählt!

  • Who if not you?: Wenn nicht du die Ärmel hochkrempelst und Dinge anpackst – wer dann?

Requirements

Deine Rolle bei uns:

Du bist Owner des Tagesgeschäfts am POS. Du berichtest an unseren Teamlead Operations und arbeitest eng mit dem Retail-Team und dem POS-Projektmanagement zusammen. Dein Erfolg ist messbar: am Anteil einwandfreier Theken, an der Zeit von der Schadensmeldung bis zur Reparatur und an termingerecht abgenommenen Umbauten.

Deine Aufgaben sind:

  • Du baust und führst unser Thekenregister mit Standort, Zustand und Historie jeder Theke, als Grundlage für alle Entscheidungen am POS.

  • Du verantwortest die Ersatzteilversorgung von der Bedarfsmeldung bis zum bestätigten Einbau in der Filiale.

  • Du planst und steuerst Umbauten und Sortimentswechsel, vom Planogramm über das Agenturbriefing bis zur Abnahme.

  • Du nimmst jede Umsetzung ab und gibst Mängel zurück, bis sie behoben sind.

  • Du bist erste Anlaufstelle für Meldungen aus den Filialen, misst die Lösungszeit und senkst sie.

  • Du organisierst Rücknahme und Aufarbeitung ausgetauschter Möbelteile und hältst Guidelines und Schulungsunterlagen für die Feldteams aktuell.

  • Du gestaltest, wie das Setup skaliert: Standards, Kennzahlen, Automatisierung.

Was du mitbringst:

  • Du hast mehrere Jahre operative POS- oder Merchandising-Arbeit im filialisierten Handel verantwortet, auf Marken-, Agentur- oder Handelsseite.

  • Du kannst an einem Beispiel belegen, wie du einen Zustand über Monate stabil gehalten hast, statt einmal aufzuräumen.

  • Du bist gelegentlich für Store-Checks in Filialen in Deutschland unterwegs und siehst dort, was auf Fotos nicht auffällt.

  • Du bist sicher in Sheets, Excel oder Airtable, sprichst fließend Deutsch und sehr gutes Englisch.

Idealerweise bringst du außerdem mit:

  • Erfahrung mit Beauty-/Kosmetik-Theken oder im Drogeriekanal.

  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung von Merchandising-Agenturen (inkl. SLA).

  • Erfahrung in der Ersatzteil- bzw. Möbellogistik.

  • Erfahrung mit einem Asset-Register oder ähnlicher Datenpflege.

  • Erfahrung mit Airtable, ClickUp oder Foto-Reporting-Tools.

Was wir dir bieten:

  • 🇪🇺 100 % Remote in Deutschland: Remote-first mit optionalem Büro in Berlin. Dazu kommen gelegentliche Store-Checks in Filialen innerhalb Deutschlands.

  • ⏱️ Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Somit kannst du privates und berufliches flexibel und entspannt vereinbaren.

  • 🚉 Deutschlandticket: Für mehr Flexibilität und Mobilität.

  • 🏃‍♀️ Urban Sports Club Membership: Weil wir wissen, wie wichtig physische Gesundheit und Ausgleich ist.

  • 🤝 Ownership: Durch viel Vertrauen & Gestaltungsspielraum hast du direkten Einfluss auf den Erfolg unseres Unternehmens und gestaltest maßgeblich unser Wachstum mit.

  • 🌴 Workation: Deine Möglichkeit Urlaub und Arbeit zu verbinden.

  • 📈Wachstumschancen: Sowohl persönlich als auch beruflich. Bei uns kannst du dich weiterentwickeln und neue Wege gehen, unterstützt durch ein jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget.

  • 🎉 Team-Events: Wir laden alle Mitarbeiter:innen regelmäßig nach Berlin ein, um eine gute Zeit zusammen zu haben und noch besser connecten zu können.

  • 🖥️ Home-Office Ausstattung: Wir übernehmen deine komplette Ausstattung, damit du auch zu Hause direkt durchstarten kannst.

  • ✈️ Individuelles Travelbudget: Für deine Besuche in Berlin, um gemeinsam mit dem Team aus dem Office zu arbeiten.

  • ✨Eine Kultur, die inspiriert: Bei uns zählt jeder Einzelne. Flache Hierarchien, schnelle Entscheidungen und echte Teamarbeit stehen im Mittelpunkt.

Challenge accepted? Dann bewirb dich jetzt und werde Teil eines Teams, das große Ziele verfolgt und dabei nie den Spaß verliert.

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

jobs.title: CRM Manager
jobs.excerpt: At Bondora, our mission is simple: to make finance easy, transparent, and accessible for everyone.
jobs.description:
At Bondora, our mission is simple: to make finance easy, transparent, and accessible for everyone.

Founded in 2008, we’ve helped more than 700,000 customers across Europe borrow and invest effortlessly through our trusted digital products.

As a rapidly growing financial technology company, we’re reaching new heights with a bold vision. We’re set to acquire a banking license, unlocking a world of possibilities for our customers. This transition will allow us to expand our lending across more EU countries and broaden our product suite to deliver even more value.

Join us on this journey and let’s build the future of finance together!

What is this role about? 🚀

As a CRM Manager, you build and run the customer journeys that guide Bondora’s customers through their whole lifecycle: from their first loan application and onboarding, to repeat loans and add-ons, to the moments when repayments get difficult. You’ll be one of three CRM Managers in Bondora’s CRM & Customer Value team, reporting to the Head of CRM & Customer Value. Our CRM runs on Braze, with unusually rich customer and loan data and value signals already flowing in. You’ll decide what to build by its value in loans and euros, prove what works against holdout groups, and treat every customer fairly: a loan is a financial decision, not a shopping cart.

Your main responsibilities 🎯

  • Build and run customer journeys in Braze across the lifecycle: application and onboarding, repeat loans and add-ons, reactivation, and payment difficulty, with QA before every launch and zero customer-facing errors.
  • Design journeys around the customer’s situation: triggers, timing, cadence, channels and fallback, stop rules, and handovers to self-service, a human or another journey.
  • Prove what works: build a control or holdout into every journey and report results as business outcomes (signed loans, revenue, arrears), not opens or clicks.
  • Prioritise by value: size opportunities in loans and euros before building, and rank your work by value rather than volume.
  • Own compliance and risk suppression: classify messages correctly, respect consent, never send commercial messages to customers showing payment risk, and involve Legal and Risk before launch.
  • Keep the data reliable: validate events and attributes, fix journeys that act on wrong or late data, and escalate upstream issues with evidence.
  • Move legacy communications into Braze and work through the team’s shared rules: one intake route for requests, and clean handovers with the other CRM Managers.

What would ensure success in this role?💪

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in CRM or lifecycle marketing. Experience in lending, fintech or recurring-revenue businesses is a plus.
  • Hands-on production experience in Braze or a comparable platform (Iterable, Customer.io, Salesforce Marketing Cloud): journeys, segmentation, event and API triggers, dynamic content and QA. You build it yourself, not through an agency.
  • Experience designing journeys for different lifecycle stages, built around the customer’s situation rather than a fixed sequence.
  • Experimentation literacy: you design tests with holdouts, read business outcomes rather than open rates, and can pull your own data (SQL or a product analytics tool).
  • Commercial judgment: you can estimate what an improvement is worth in loans and euros and decide what to build first.
  • Sound compliance judgment: transactional vs. promotional messages, consent, and responsible treatment of customers in a credit business.
  • A habit of checking data before trusting it, and of fixing problems at the root.
  • Working expertise in email, SMS and WhatsApp, with modular, localisable content for several markets.
  • A habit of using AI to speed up QA and analysis, with the judgment to know when not to trust it.
  • High ownership and a bias to action: you’d rather ship something good this week than something perfect next quarter, and you drive conversations with Product, Engineering, Legal and Risk toward decisions.

What can you expect at Bondora?

  • Contribute to Bondora’s ambitious goal of reaching 1BN in revenue. Your skills and efforts will directly impact our growth trajectory and shape the future of our company.
  • Our employees deserve the best. We recognize our people with a competitive salary and a generous benefits package (5 weeks of vacation, private healthcare compensation, hobby grant, mental healthcare support, share options and much more!)
  • We provide an environment that encourages your personal and professional growth. As we constantly evolve and innovate, you’ll have endless opportunities (and budget) to expand your skills and skyrocket your career.

The next steps

If you have the guts, ideas, and a team vision, apply now!

Our hiring process:

1️⃣ Meet Anna, our Recruiter — your first chat to share your story and ambitions.
2️⃣ Meet Mario, CMO.
3️⃣ Tackle a home task to showcase your skills.
4️⃣ Complete our personality and logic assessments via Alva Labs.
5️⃣ Meet Pärtel Tomberg, our CEO.
6️⃣ Bar Raiser interview with Olga Kikas, our Chief of People.
7️⃣ 🎉 If the stars align — welcome to Bondora!

Join our team of Bondorians, and let's make it happen!

Proximie is on a mission to improve healthcare by transforming the world’s operating rooms into connected ecosystems of people, devices, and data.

Proximie is seeking a Director, Performance Enablement to run the planning, measurement, and execution disciplines that will scale our Americas Delivery organization. Reporting to the Vice President, Delivery & Operations, Americas, this role owns the shared Delivery operating system: portfolio reviews, demand and capacity forecasting, performance reporting, risk and dependency tracking, decision follow-through, and delivery economics.

The VP sets Delivery strategy, structure, and priorities. The Director turns those priorities into operating plans and reliable information, helping functional leaders deliver consistently and keeping the Voice of Customer present across functions.

The ideal candidate pairs analytical operating expertise with sound customer and executive judgment. Our Story

TopDog Law is a nationally scaling personal injury firm that owns the client experience end to end, from marketing and intake through litigation. We've grown 2-3x year over year for three years running, and we're now building the operations, systems, and teams to scale without sacrificing quality or culture. We're fully remote, and we value ownership, open communication, and speed. If you want to help build something exceptional, you'll feel at home here.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Staff-level Software Engineer who is as comfortable designing production systems as they are applying AI to real business problems. This is a hybrid role, not a pure AI research or ML engineering position. You'll build the internal tools and platforms that power our operations teams, and be the technical expert on where AI creates real value and where it doesn't.

You'll set technical direction across multiple teams and systems, not just the ones you build yourself. When the business needs to explore an AI opportunity, weigh technology options, or understand where we stand on AI, you'll investigate, recommend, and deliver. You'll navigate ambiguity and make well-reasoned build-versus-buy decisions, then drive the recommended solution through implementation. You'll also think about the data each product generates, so what we build feeds our analytics and helps leadership decide where to invest.

You bring strong engineering judgment, a bias toward pragmatic solutions, and the ability to turn open-ended questions into decisions and working software. You'll be a trusted technical advisor to leadership, and your impact will be measured by what the whole team ships, not just what you build yourself.

What You Will Own

Architecture & Delivery

  • Build and own. Architect and build internal tools and platforms for operations teams, owning them from design through deployment and ongoing operation, including reliability and incident follow-through.
  • Set direction. Define service boundaries, integration patterns, and data flow across teams, and write the technical strategy and RFCs that make the direction clear.
  • Simplify. Reduce operational toil by retiring or consolidating systems, managing tech debt and migrations, and weighing long-term maintenance cost in every build-versus-buy decision.
  • Integrate and protect. Build reliable integrations with legacy and third-party SaaS systems, with security, access control, and audit trails designed in for sensitive data.

Applied AI

  • Apply AI with judgment. Identify where AI belongs in a solution and where it doesn't, and design it as a well-engineered part of the system (retrieval, agents, LLM-powered features, workflow automation).
  • Prove it, then ship it. Run time-boxed proofs of concept that answer "is this worth doing?" with evidence, then advance successful proofs of concept into production-ready solutions, with evaluation, observability, reliability, and security.
  • Guide AI investment. Assess our AI maturity, define a practical roadmap, and track AI cost and ROI so investment decisions rest on data.

Data

  • Build products that produce good data. Design data models and instrumentation so every product generates clean, usable data for analytics and strategic planning.

Technical Leadership

  • Lead across competing priorities. Align teams with differing priorities on shared platforms, standards, and tradeoffs. Build consensus through influence and evidence, and drive decisions when consensus cannot be reached.
  • Improve engineering quality and delivery practices. Write high-quality code and lead through code reviews, design reviews, and engineering standards, using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) to raise the whole team's delivery speed.
  • Mentor and advise. Mentor engineers and serve as a trusted technical advisor to stakeholders and leadership, explaining tradeoffs clearly and driving decisions to closure.

What You Bring

Required:

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of designing and shipping reliable, maintainable production systems.
  • Demonstrated Staff or Principal-level scope: you have led architecture or a major technical initiative across multiple teams with competing priorities, and aligned them on shared platforms or standards.
  • Hands-on experience building applications with LLMs and generative AI in production, not just experiments. Demonstrate experience operating AI systems at scale, addressing production challenges, and measuring outcomes.
  • Working experience rolling out agentic systems into production, including evaluation, guardrails, and monitoring.
  • Strong backend and systems design skills, including APIs, data modeling, cloud infrastructure, and integration with legacy and third-party SaaS systems.
  • Reliability engineering experience, including SLOs, idempotency, retries, partial failure handling, and data consistency across integrated systems.
  • Experience building systems that handle sensitive data, with sound security and governance practices such as access control, audit trails, and PII and privileged data handling.
  • A track record of taking ownership of essential engineering work: tech debt strategy, migrations, and deprecation of systems that are no longer worth their cost.
  • Experience designing data models and instrumentation that support analytics.
  • Working knowledge of modern AI application patterns: RAG, embeddings, vector search, prompt, harness, and context engineering, tool use and agents, and evaluation methods.
  • Ability to weigh build-versus-buy tradeoffs and balance technical options against cost, complexity, and business value, including choosing simpler solutions or stopping projects when the evidence doesn't support them.
  • Strong communication skills, including explaining AI concepts and tradeoffs to non-technical audiences and driving decisions to closure.

Preferred (Nice to Have):

  • Experience with vector databases and search technologies, whether managed services or extensions to existing databases.
  • Experience with a modern data stack (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake, dbt) and building the data pipelines that feed analytics.
  • Experience building internal tools or platforms for operations teams.
  • Familiarity with ML fundamentals, fine-tuning, or model evaluation frameworks.
  • Experience with AI cost management, such as token usage, model selection, and caching.
  • Background in a regulated or document-heavy industry such as legal or financial services.

Who Thrives Here (Core Values)

We don't hire on resumes alone. We hire for competence, character, and mindset.

What We Offer

  • Experience with motion design or microinteractions that improve usability
  • Experience facilitating design-thinking workshops or design sprints, or working with front-end component libraries and design-to-code workflows

Job Description:

Overview

Baker Tilly’s Industrial Advisory team partners with manufacturing and distribution clients to solve complex operational and financial challenges through data-driven insights and strategic advisory services. Our professionals help clients improve operational performance, evaluate capital investments, optimize profitability, and leverage technology to drive better business decisions.

As a Senior Manager, you’ll collaborate with teams across Baker Tilly to solve complex operational challenges and deliver high impact solutions. This role will involve heavy collaboration with clients, often working alongside them to help build value.

We are seeking a candidate who has hands-on experience developing and executing manufacturing cost accounting, inventory costing, and related systems and processes. The ideal candidate will have experience designing, implementing, managing, or advising on cost-accounting processes within manufacturing organizations and will be comfortable working with detailed product, manufacturing, purchasing, and inventory data.

Our clients require subject matter expertise from professionals who understand how products are manufactured, how manufacturing costs flow through an organization, and how accounting processes, ERP systems, operational data, and management reporting work together.

This individual will also provide senior leadership for the cost-accounting and data-analysis components of Baker Tilly’s domestic content consulting services.

Successful candidates will be expected to take ownership of assigned engagements, exercise sound professional judgment, and move work forward with limited day-to-day oversight. The successful candidate will be proactive, resourceful, and able to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

As one of the fastest growing firms in the nation, Baker Tilly has the ability to offer you upward career trajectory, flexibility in how and where you get your work done and meaningful relationships with clients, teammates and leadership who truly care about you and your development.

Key Responsibilities:

Inventory and Manufacturing Cost Advisory

  • Lead consulting engagements involving inventory costing, product costing, manufacturing cost analysis, and related financial and operational processes.
  • Assess client cost-accounting methodologies, systems, processes, controls, and data and identify opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency, transparency, and management decision-making.
  • Provide subject matter expertise in areas including:
  • Standard and actual costing
  • Inventory valuation
  • Bills of material and manufacturing routings
  • Direct material and direct labor costs
  • Manufacturing overhead and cost allocations
  • Purchase price, material, labor, and manufacturing variances
  • Inventory controls and cycle-counting programs
  • Product and component cost structures
  • ERP costing and material-flow processes
  • Cost and profitability reporting
  • Work with clients and ERP or technology teams to evaluate and improve cost-accounting processes and system configurations, including material-flow logic and product-costing methodologies.
  • Design and oversee analyses of manufacturing costs, purchasing activity, inventory, variances, product profitability, and other financial and operational information.
  • Develop practical methodologies for complex costing situations where client systems or available data do not readily provide the information required.
  • Document and analyze client processes, internal controls, data flows, and workflows and recommend improvements.

Domestic Content Cost Consulting

  • Provide senior leadership for the cost-accounting and financial-data components of domestic content consulting engagements.
  • Work directly with manufacturers, suppliers, and client teams to obtain the detailed product, cost, and sourcing information necessary to perform domestic content analyses.
  • Evaluate and analyze bills of material, supplier information, purchasing records, labor and routing data, manufacturing overhead, inventory records, product costs, and other manufacturing information.
  • Develop methodologies for identifying, categorizing, and calculating domestic and non-domestic manufacturing costs or content in accordance with the requirements applicable to each engagement.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and limitations in manufacturer or supplier data and develop reasonable and supportable approaches to address those issues.
  • Assist clients in developing repeatable processes, controls, and documentation for collecting and maintaining information needed to support domestic content requirements.
  • Coordinate with Baker Tilly professionals in tax, incentives, government contracting, engineering, supply chain, legal, technology, and other specialties as appropriate.
  • Review analyses and supporting documentation to ensure conclusions are accurate, consistent, and defensible to client management and other stakeholders.

Engagement and Client Leadership

  • Develop engagement approaches, work plans, staffing models, budgets, milestones, data requests, and deliverables.
  • Manage multiple concurrent engagements while maintaining quality, timeliness, and engagement economics.
  • Serve as a senior client contact and build trusted relationships with finance, accounting, operations, procurement, supply-chain, engineering, and executive leadership.
  • Lead client interviews, working sessions, data discussions, executive presentations, and findings meetings.
  • Translate complex manufacturing, accounting, and data issues into clear business implications and actionable recommendations.
  • Exercise professional judgment when client data is incomplete, inconsistent, or unavailable and guide teams in developing appropriate analytical approaches.
  • Review team analyses and deliverables for technical accuracy, quality, clarity, and completeness.

Team Leadership and Practice Development

  • Provide on-the-job coaching and technical guidance in manufacturing cost accounting, inventory costing, data analysis, and domestic content methodologies.
  • Identify opportunities to expand services and deliver additional value to manufacturing and distribution clients.
  • Demonstrate an entrepreneurial mindset by identifying emerging client needs and developing new service offerings and solutions.
  • Participate in business-development activities, including prospect discussions, development of scopes of work, proposals, presentations, and fee estimates.
  • Build relationships across Baker Tilly to bring the appropriate combination of technical and industry expertise to client engagements.
  • Contribute to thought leadership, articles, presentations, and other market-development activities.
  • Travel as needed to client offices and manufacturing facilities.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 4-year degree
  • 8 years professional experience

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in accounting or finance
  • 10+ years of experience in the accounting or finance department of manufacturing companies orconsulting firms supporting inventory costprojects
  • Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and/or Certified Management Accountant certifications
  • Deep understanding of manufacturing cost-accounting concepts, including standard and actual costing, inventory valuation, bills of material, routings, material and labor costs, manufacturing overhead, allocations, and manufacturing variances.
  • Experience obtaining, validating, and analyzing detailed cost and operational data from manufacturing facilities, suppliers, or other third parties.
  • Experience designing, implementing, or improving cost-accounting processes and methodologies within manufacturing organizations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to develop practical solutions when available data is incomplete or inconsistent.
  • Experience building pro forma financial models incorporating income statements and cash flows to support business decisions
  • Demonstrates an entrepreneurial mindset to identify client needs and build, plan, and manage services to support those needs
  • Experience building processes within SAP or Oracle Finance and Inventory Management Platforms
  • Prior experience with domestic content, manufacturing incentives, government contracting, tax incentives, country-of-origin analysis, or similar product-level cost and sourcing requirements is beneficial but not required.

The US National pay rate range for this job position is $179,850-$340,970. Actual compensation is influenced by a variety of relevant factors including but not limited to applicant’s skills, prior experience, qualifications, degrees, professional certifications, work arrangements and geographic location. Baker Tilly offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package to eligible employees.

Who We Are

As the leading Neuro-Contextual Advertising Company, we combine Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and neuroscience to understand not only what content is about, but how it makes people feel and what they intend to do next.

Our proprietary AI, Liz, enables brands to connect with audiences across the open web and Connected TV without cookies or user tracking. Your Challenge

Our Core Values

Outcome over Output
We measure success by impact and value, not by volume of features or lines of code.

We Are All Scouts
We take ownership and leave things better than we found them.

Data informs our decisions and helps us continuously improve our systems and results.

Tech Stack

Why Join Seedtag?

jobs.title: Director of People
jobs.excerpt: WHO ARE WE? Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company.
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

Base salary: $170,000 to $190,000. Plus an annual bonus paid as a flat amount rather than a percentage of base.

Launch Potato is about 200 people, profitable, and growing. The performance management system that got us here was built by our SVP of Talent, and he still runs it. That system becomes yours.

You're inheriting something that works. There's a levels framework, a rating scale, a calibration process, and managers who have been through several cycles. It got us to 200 people. Your job is deciding what carries forward and change-managing the rest, across an org that moves fast and adopts new processes.

We want someone who'll find the version that works and then hold it there while the company gets good at it.

If you want to own a function, make it extraordinary, and be judged on whether it actually got better, keep reading.

Why This Seat

  • Real ownership, immediately. Performance, total rewards, and compliance are yours to own rather than support. You'll defend a compensation number in front of a CFO who checks it.
  • An SVP who wants to hand this over. Not one who says that and then rewrites your deck. The explicit goal is that the HR function runs without him.
  • Executive reach by default. Calibration and leveling decisions live with the C-suite, and you present your own work. You won't spend year one convincing anyone that performance management matters.
  • Leverage is part of the mandate, not a side project. We are tech-first and AI-forward, which means we can run lean teams and do more with less. You'll push that further, build the tooling managers actually open, and make everything easier without taking substance out of it. Nobody will ask you to do it the slow way.

How This Team Is Led

From Kris Osborne, SVP of Talent.

I'll tell you what I want and what the constraints are and then get out of the way. I don't rewrite people's work. If I disagree with where you landed you'll hear it from me early, and if you still think you're right then push back, because I'd rather change my mind than have you go quiet and build something you don't believe in.

I ask before I decide. When something changes the shape of this team the people on it hear it from me first and they get a real say in it, not a heads up after it's done.

I care about the outcome and I'm not going to do your job for you. Bring me a problem and I'll work it with you, but I'm not going to take it off your plate and hand it back finished.

I'm hiring this seat because I want someone we can all learn from. Bring me a better answer than mine and I'll take it.

What You'll Bring

All required.

  • A full performance cycle you owned end to end, not supported. Owned more than once, at 150 people or more. Design, timeline, manager prep, calibration, rollout, retro.
  • Compensation and benefits you've owned. Band design, benchmarking methodology, benefits renewals, the annual comp cycle. You can defend a number to a CFO.
  • HR compliance as standing scope, not as a project. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. You've inherited a backlog and cleared it.
  • A people system that outlasted you. Built, adopted, and still recognizable two cycles later.
  • Leverage you built that people adopted. You've automated or rebuilt part of a people process so it ran faster, the quality held or improved, and the team actually used it. Adoption is the test here, the same way durability is the test above.
  • Experience taking a company our size to materially larger, on headcount or revenue, more than once. You know what breaks first at the next stage because you've watched it break.
  • Empowered your team to raise the bar. You have clear examples of coaching, mentoring, and growing a team that created extraordinary outcomes.

This is a player-coach seat. Managers here lead a team and deliver work personally, at every level.

Nice to Have

  • You have opinions about what performance management gets wrong, and specific examples of what you changed
  • You can tell a process problem from a manager-capability problem, and you fix the right one
  • You're the person who says the uncomfortable thing in a calibration room

What You'll Own

Performance management. The mid-year and annual cycles end to end: design, timeline, communication, execution. What the cycle needs to produce and what to cut. A timeline published early enough that managers plan around it. The retro after each one, and the judgment about when a change is warranted and when to leave it alone.

Total rewards. Band design and the benchmarking methodology behind it. Benefits renewals and the economics underneath them. The annual comp cycle, with leveling and pay kept connected.

Compliance. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. The current backlog, plus the escalation and coverage protocols that follow it.

Manager enablement. Preparing managers for real performance conversations, including the one where someone rated themselves higher than their manager did. The calibration process, including where two managers apply the same bar differently. Playbooks and self-service resources so a manager gets an answer without booking a meeting. Standing support for the roughly three dozen front-line managers who get it reactively today.

Leverage and tooling. Finding the parts of everything above that shouldn't be done by hand, and fixing them. Building what a manager will actually open rather than what looks good in a demo. Taking time out of the cycle while the conversations get better rather than thinner.

jobs.excerpt: About Redesign Group The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation.
jobs.description:
About Redesign Group

The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation. Our globally diverse team members, partnerships with strategic technology manufacturers, and cybersecurity services position us to be a business partner that’s ready for what’s next.

We live by our core values of operating in the service of others, being problem solvers, and focusing on long term partnerships. You’ll excel at Redesign if you thrive in a rewarding environment that moves quickly, challenges you to grow and fosters collaboration. We seek candidates with a hands-on customer-first approach, robust interpersonal and communication skills, strong work ethic and excellent time management. While teamwork is expected, the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment is crucial.

Job Description

The Senior Tooling and Automation Engineer is a hands-on builder who owns how the Managed Services tooling ecosystem works as one connected system. You will write the integrations, automations, skills, and apps that link our RMM, network monitoring, backup reporting, and service management platforms, using AI-assisted development as your primary way of producing code. You will own Jira Service Management configuration end to end, own the alerting lifecycle so the team acts only on meaningful signals, and serve as the senior escalation point when any piece of tooling fails.

Each core platform has an administrator who runs it day to day; you own the connective layer between them and the standards for how they alert, integrate, and roll out to customers, and you work with each administrator on changes inside their tool. Where the stack has a gap, you lead the build-or-buy decision from business justification through evaluation and rollout. We will ask you to show working code you have built with AI assistance, because that is how this job gets done.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain integrations between platforms using APIs, webhooks, and email, writing the connecting code, skills, and apps with AI-assisted development tools.
  • Own Jira Service Management configuration, including screens, workflows, custom ticket and request types, automations, and queues.
  • Identify noise across the alerting cycle, human and system, and tune the stack so only actionable alerts reach the team.
  • Serve as the senior escalation point for tooling failures, including broken integrations, misbehaving automation, authored scripts, and alerts firing on false positives.
  • Set and enforce the standards for how core tooling integrates and alerts, working with each platform's administrator on changes inside their tool.
  • Identify gaps in the tooling stack and lead the build-or-buy decision, including business justification, evaluation, and end-to-end rollout of new tools.
  • Ensure every customer's tooling is fully rolled out and tuned to their environment, including custom OS patching and observability alerting policies agreed with the customer.
  • Explain our tooling to customers in plain terms: what it does, how it installs, and its impact on their environment.
  • Produce service level objective, utilization, and operational reporting for delivery leadership from tooling data.
  • Execute all work within an ITIL-aligned change management framework and keep integrations, automations, and configuration documented so the environment is auditable and not dependent on one person.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Demonstrated fluency with AI-assisted coding tools (Claude, Cursor, Replit, or similar) to produce working, maintainable code, with examples you can walk us through.
  • Hands-on experience building integrations using REST APIs, webhooks, and structured data (JSON, XML), including common authentication methods.
  • Scripting and development capability in a language such as Python, PowerShell, or JavaScript, with working use of Git for source control.
  • Experience administering Jira Service Management or a comparable ITSM platform, including workflows, request types, and automations.
  • Working knowledge of RMM, network monitoring, and backup tooling, and experience tuning alerting to cut noise.
  • Solid understanding of ITIL and change management, with the ability to execute within a structured framework.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across platforms, integrations, and automation, and a clear, customer-facing communication style.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with NinjaOne, Auvik, Bocada Cloud, or Jira Service Management.
  • Experience leading tool evaluations and vendor selection, including proof-of-concept work and business justification.
  • Familiarity with workflow-automation or iPaaS platforms.

Background

  • 5+ years in an MSP or enterprise IT environment focused on tooling, automation, or systems integration, in roles where you built and owned the integrations rather than only used the tools.
  • Experience as the first or only person responsible for a whole tooling stack, since each of our core platforms already has an administrator and you will set the standard rather than inherit one.
  • Bachelor's degree in information technology or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match (annual dollar cap applied)
  • Flexible time off plan
  • 15 paid holidays
  • Sick leave (amount varies by state requirements and is at least the minimum required by any state)
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Life insurance
  • Paid parental leave

We’re an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. We consider qualified candidates without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, the compensation range for this role is included, with final pay based on experience, skills, and location. We participate in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process—just let us know how we can help.

jobs.excerpt: Who we areneuefische GmbH, with its brands neuefische and Spiced Academy, has been Germany’s leading provider of technology bootcamps for 10 years.
jobs.description:
Who we are

neuefische GmbH, with its brands neuefische and Spiced Academy, has been Germany’s leading provider of technology bootcamps for 10 years.

Our programs empower people to pursue careers they love and drive skills transformation across Germany. To date, we’ve trained over 7,000 participants, with around 70% finding a job right after graduation.

With more than 40% women in our courses, we foster not only talent but also diversity in tech. Many of our programs also include certifications from IHK, Amazon, CompTIA, and other key partners.

Our vision: to transform lives by equipping people with the skills, confidence, and support to succeed in tech—delivered through outstanding teaching both online and on campus, in German and English.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Subject Matter Expert (SME) with a technical Product Management background, gained building AI products in close collaboration with engineering and data teams.
Our teaching team has already redesigned the curriculum of our 16-week AI Product Management course, with learning objectives defined for every session. The SME will complete the content: building new learning materials, updating existing ones, and creating the exercises, case labs and assessments that bring the curriculum to life.

This is a revamp, not a new product: much of the content already exists in our current course and sister programmes and needs to be reshaped to the new objectives.
We expect the work to be done AI-assisted (for example with Claude), which is what makes the timeline realistic.

This person must be hands-on, structured and accountable for quality, and a team player who stays in close, constant communication with our teaching team.
The content prepares learners, a mixed cohort of product and product-adjacent professionals, not all of them technical but also expected to get technical knowledge during the course, to work as AI Product and Project Managers.

The content goes well beyond theory or tool usage. It will enable learners to:

  • Discover, frame and prioritise AI opportunities, and decide when AI is the right solution and when it is not

  • Design AI experiences with clear fallbacks, human review and success metrics

  • Work confidently with engineering and data teams: read data, run experiments, and evaluate models, LLM outputs, RAG systems and agents

  • Make cost, risk and compliance decisions (EU AI Act, GDPR) and take AI features from prototype to launch and operations

Graduates should be able to own an AI feature end to end, closing the gap between understanding AI and shipping it responsibly.

What is already in place

  • The redesigned curriculum: 12 teaching weeks with 81 sessions, plus a 4-week team capstone

  • Defined primary and secondary learning objectives for each session, and a rework status (Create new, Deepen, Reduce, Keep)

  • Existing course materials, plus relevant materials from two sister programmes (Product Management with AI, Digital & AI Transformation Management)

  • House templates and a teaching team that reviews each content batch (expected tools: Slidev, Github, Noiton, Miro)

How we work

  • Kickoff with the teaching team to agree priorities, formats and templates

  • First batch of about one week of course content, with in-depth feedback; after that you work independently in batches delivered on a weekly frequency and aligned in calls with the team.

  • Review meeting and revision rounds

  • Shared technical work: for statistics and other technical topics, the teaching team proposes examples or builds parts directly, so you can focus on the product perspective

  • Fixed project budget, not hourly;

Core tasks

  1. Plan the content per session. Review the existing and sister-programme materials and propose, for each session, what to reuse, adapt or build, including how to resolve topic overlaps across the curriculum.

  2. Build new session content . Create new: lecture, pre-work exercise and solution for every session against the objectives already defined.

  3. Update existing content. Deepen sessions with the AI PM angle and new exercises.

  4. Build high-impact practical tasks and assessments. Case labs with realistic, synthetic and GDPR-safe datasets; project briefs with templates, rubrics and sample deliverables.

  5. Write a coach page for every session so any instructor can teach it: objectives, run sheet with timings, key messages and common learner questions following the company’s standards and provided templates.

  6. Keep the content industry-relevant and future-ready, reflecting current AI product practice, tools such as Claude Code, and the evolving regulatory landscape.

Required

  • Proven hands-on Product Management experience, including shipping AI or ML-powered features in production in close collaboration with engineering and data teams

  • Practical fluency in the product side of AI: opportunity assessment, AI UX and fallbacks, metrics and experimentation, AI cost and vendor decisions, launch and monitoring

  • Comfortable with the technical basics the course teaches non-technical learners: SQL, Python notebooks (pandas), statistics, A/B testing, causality, Marketing Mixed Models, Git, and AI-assisted tools such as Claude Code

  • Highly proficient in AI-assisted content production (for example with Claude): you turn learning objectives into slides, exercises and examples quickly, while owning their accuracy

  • Strong communicator and team player, comfortable working in short feedback loops with a teaching team

  • Prior experience in course development or professional training, ideally for bootcamp or career-changer audiences, is highly preferred

  • Working knowledge of the EU AI Act and GDPR in a product context is a plus

  • Fluent written English; German is a plus

* Even if you feel like ticking only 60% of the requirements, we would still like to review your application. At neuefische, we attach great importance to equal opportunities and respectful cooperation. All applicants should be valued equally - regardless of gender and gender identity, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age, sexual orientation and identity. We value diversity and we are committed to integration and diversity.

What We Offer 🌱

👩‍🎓 An opportunity to join one of the fastest-growing companies in Tech-Education

🪴 A platform to grow as a part of a team of dedicated professionals

🎉 International, passionate (and fun) working environment

Job Summary

ServiceNow Technical Project Manager

Employment: Full-time | Location: Remote; Eastern Time business hours

The ServiceNow Technical Project Manager at Aptive Resources LLC supports the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program and the CPMO Data Analytics and Insights team. This role leads ServiceNow enhancements, sustainment, integrations, and reporting supporting the Tiered Hub Process and enterprise issue resolution.

The role combines technical project management, senior business analysis, and Agile leadership with practical ServiceNow solution design and configuration expertise. Working with government leads, developers, architects, QA, analytics teams, and field stakeholders, the Technical PM translates business and policy requirements into functional solutions and manages delivery from requirements through deployment, adoption, and operational support.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Technical and Agile delivery leadership. Maintain roadmaps, project plans, capacity forecasts, milestones, and risk, issue, and dependency logs. Partner with technical leads and the Scrum Master on PI planning, Agile coaching, sprint commitments, and multi-sprint release sequencing; resolve impediments and communicate delivery tradeoffs.
  • Business analysis and backlog management. Facilitate stakeholder workshops and translate business, operational, and policy needs into process maps, functional designs, Jira epics, stories, and acceptance criteria. Maintain traceability and obtain required government and Change Control Board approvals before committing scope.
  • Functional design and technical coordination. Guide and contribute to low-code/no-code configuration of request forms, approval workflows, self-service capabilities, notifications, dashboards, and integrations. Partner with developers and architects to assess technical designs, estimates, data models, and platform impacts; resolve dependencies across configuration and custom development.
  • Enhancements and process alignment. Lead approved improvements to EHRM Request workflows, Informatics Patient Safety and Health Services forms, and VistA/CPRS request processes and transitions. Ensure delivery addresses routing, usability, submission accuracy, data integrity, and alignment with the Tiered Hub Process.
  • API and integration delivery. Coordinate API requirements, architecture reviews, service-account provisioning, access approvals, development, testing, and documentation. Align required tables and variables with downstream analytics and integration needs, including Power BI and Databricks dependencies.
  • Reporting and data quality. Manage delivery of ServiceNow-native reports, dashboards, KPIs, and Performance Analytics enhancements. Partner with analytics leads to validate definitions, source data, filters, and role-based visibility; maintain reporting inventory and resolve discrepancies affecting operational or leadership reporting.
  • Testing and release readiness. Coordinate QA, user acceptance testing, regression testing, defect triage, release documentation, and deployment readiness. Confirm acceptance evidence, required approvals, communication plans, and post-release validation before closing delivery commitments.
  • Sustainment, readiness, and adoption. Coordinate maintenance, user and assignment-group updates, routing changes, and support requests. Track site readiness checklists, training, communications, and go-live support. Monitor post-deployment usage and field feedback to identify adoption barriers and prioritize improvements.
  • Governance and executive communication. Coordinate VA OIT architecture, security, change, and deployment reviews. Translate policy requirements into documented platform controls, including role-based access and identity governance. Maintain decision records and technical documentation; brief government leaders on delivery, risks, and decisions needed.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Education. Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Healthcare IT, Project Management, or a related discipline; equivalent education and experience may be considered where permitted by the applicable labor category, contract, and customer requirements.
  • Experience. At least 5 years in enterprise IT delivery, technical project management, business analysis, or Agile team leadership, including at least 3 years supporting ServiceNow implementation, enhancement, or sustainment. Experience must include coordinating cross-functional delivery and leading requirements, backlog, or release activities.
  • ServiceNow technical depth. Practical experience with ServiceNow functional solution design and configuration, request and incident lifecycles, workflow automation, self-service capabilities, data models, and access controls. Working knowledge of integrations and REST APIs; ability to evaluate technical designs, estimates, dependencies, and release risks with engineering teams.
  • Delivery lifecycle. Demonstrated experience leading requirements definition, backlog refinement, development coordination, QA/UAT, deployment, stabilization, and ongoing support. Ability to manage competing enhancement and operational priorities while maintaining scope, quality, and accountability.
  • Agile and project tools. Proficiency with Jira and Agile/Scrum delivery, including team coaching, story development, acceptance criteria, sprint reviews, and release planning. Experience using delivery and documentation tools such as Azure DevOps, ServiceNow Agile, Confluence, SharePoint, and Microsoft Office.
  • Reporting literacy. Ability to translate business questions into reporting requirements and measurable KPIs, assess data quality and dashboard accuracy, and manage dependencies between ServiceNow-native reporting and external analytics teams.
  • Regulated delivery and communication. Experience coordinating technology delivery in a regulated environment. Strong facilitation, problem-solving, written communication, and executive briefing skills; ability to explain technical issues and delivery tradeoffs to nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Citizenship and access. U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain required VA suitability and system access, including Public Trust requirements.

Desired Qualifications

  • Direct experience supporting VA ServiceNow, EHRM, CPMO, or federal healthcare programs, including familiarity with VA OIT architecture, governance, change, and deployment processes.
  • Experience delivering ServiceNow solutions across ITSM and related capabilities such as IRM/GRC, CSM, SPM, ITOM, and CMDB; familiarity with enterprise ERP, CRM, SaaS, and PaaS modernization.
  • Experience with ServiceNow-native reporting and Performance Analytics, Power BI, data integrations, and operational measures such as backlog, aging, cycle time, service levels, and defect trends.
  • Experience supporting the Tiered Hub Process, facility deployments, field engagement, end-user training, and distributed Agile teams.
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA), PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I), PMP, CAD, or relevant SAFe credentials. Certifications are preferred; none is required.
  • Familiarity with generative AI, large language models, and agentic workflows for evaluating process improvement opportunities within approved governance and security requirements.
  • Current VA access and experience navigating VA onboarding and access processes.

Physical Requirements

Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for extended periods, use a computer keyboard and mouse, and communicate verbally and in writing. The employee may occasionally need to stand, walk, bend, or lift up to 15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.
