jobs.description:
Software Engineer, External Integrations & Data

Location: Remote Canada

Employment Type: Full-time

Level: Senior Software Engineer

About the company

Our Series A client is transforming the building supply industry through innovative technology. Their integrated commerce platform enables independent building suppliers to streamline operations, enhance customer service, and deliver exceptional digital buying experiences. By connecting sales, accounts receivable, operations, and customer engagement into one seamless solution, they help their customers operate more efficiently and drive growth.

Their team is made up of curious, entrepreneurial problem-solvers who thrive in a fast-paced environment. They value innovation, collaboration, and ownership, with a shared focus on building practical solutions that create meaningful impact for their customers and the industry as a whole.

About the Role

We’re looking for a resourceful Software Engineer who thrives on solving problems where the path forward isn’t always obvious. You’ll work on building systems that interact with external platforms, services, and data sources — particularly in situations where official APIs are limited, unavailable, or insufficient for the job.

This role is ideal for an engineer with experience in web scraping, reverse engineering, or building integrations with third-party systems that weren’t necessarily designed to be integrated with.

You’ll help us connect to external sources, extract and normalize messy or unstructured data, and turn it into reliable, structured information that can power modern AI-driven applications. We’re looking for someone who enjoys figuring out how things work under the hood, navigating undocumented systems, and building robust solutions to complex technical challenges.

What You’ll Do

  • Build integrations without traditional APIs: Develop systems that interact with external websites, platforms, and services when official APIs are unavailable, incomplete, or too restrictive.

  • Develop data acquisition pipelines: Collect, extract, and transform data from diverse external sources, including HTML pages, dynamic web applications, documents, and unstructured content.

  • Reverse engineer external systems: Analyze network requests, browser behavior, page structures, and undocumented interfaces to understand how external systems operate.

  • Build scraping and automation tools: Use technologies such as browser automation, HTTP clients, headless browsers, and custom extraction logic to retrieve data reliably.

  • Clean and normalize messy data: Transform inconsistent, duplicated, incomplete, or poorly structured data into clean, standardized formats suitable for downstream applications and AI workflows.

  • Build resilient systems: Design integrations that can handle changing page layouts, evolving external systems, rate limits, authentication flows, and unexpected failures.

  • Leverage AI for data processing: Explore ways to use LLMs and other AI techniques to extract, classify, enrich, validate, and structure data from unstructured sources.

  • Improve reliability and scalability: Implement monitoring, retries, validation, error handling, and automated testing to ensure integrations remain dependable over time.

  • Collaborate across engineering and product: Work with other engineers to turn ambiguous requirements and unfamiliar external systems into practical, maintainable solutions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Professional software engineering experience building production-quality applications, integrations, or data pipelines.

  • Experience with at least one of the following:

    • Web scraping or large-scale data extraction.

    • Reverse engineering or working with undocumented interfaces.

    • Building integrations with third-party platforms that lack robust APIs.

    • Extracting, transforming, and cleaning data from inconsistent external sources.

  • Strong proficiency in a language such as Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript.

  • Experience working with HTTP, REST concepts, HTML, DOM structures, JSON, .Net C# and network requests.

  • An understanding of authentication, cookies, sessions, pagination, rate limiting, and other challenges associated with external integrations.

  • Experience designing maintainable software that can adapt when external systems change.

  • Strong debugging and analytical skills, with the ability to investigate unfamiliar systems and work through ambiguous technical problems.

  • A pragmatic, resourceful mindset and a willingness to experiment, prototype, and find creative solutions.

What Success Looks Like

  • You can take an unfamiliar external platform and figure out how to retrieve the information we need, even when there isn't a straightforward API.

  • You can turn inconsistent, dirty, or unstructured external data into clean, usable, structured datasets.

  • You build integrations that remain reliable even as external systems evolve.

  • You can move from investigation and proof of concept to production-ready software without sacrificing maintainability.

  • You consistently find practical solutions to problems that don't have an obvious playbook.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a software engineer who enjoys the investigative side of engineering. They might have built scrapers, reverse-engineered web applications, developed browser automation, or created integrations with platforms that weren't designed to expose their data.

They don't necessarily need experience in every area listed above. We're more interested in someone who has demonstrated the ability to figure out how external systems work, access and interpret data, and build reliable software around systems they don't control.

This is not simply a traditional API integration role. It's an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of external systems, data acquisition, data quality, and AI

jobs.title: Active Directory / Identity Engineer (Senior)
jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks an Active Directory / Identity Engineer to own and sustain the Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services environment supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Active Directory / Identity Engineer to own and sustain the Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services environment supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This senior engineering position manages AD objects, organizational units, Group Policy Objects, trusts, replication, schema governance, delegated permissions, domain services, and recovery capabilities.

The Active Directory / Identity Engineer ensures that directory services remain secure, available, recoverable, and aligned with USMEPCOM operational and cybersecurity requirements. The engineer supports domain and forest planning, account and group administration, site replication, trust relationships, Group Policy, domain-controller lifecycle activities, backup, restoration, and modernization.

The position also evaluates and tests approved Identity, Credential, and Access Management capabilities, including potential Okta integrations and other identity-modernization technologies. These modernization activities complement—not replace—the position’s requirement for direct, hands-on AD DS engineering expertise.

The engineer works closely with cybersecurity, Service Desk, systems, cloud, network, application, COOP, and Government identity stakeholders. This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional after-hours maintenance, incident response, COOP exercises, on-site support, or travel may be required.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Active Directory / Identity Engineer will:

  • Serve as the senior technical owner for the USMEPCOM Active Directory Domain Services environment.
  • Install, configure, maintain, update, troubleshoot, and recover Active Directory services and supporting components.
  • Create, modify, disable, delete, and manage authorized AD objects in accordance with approved processes.
  • Manage organizational units, users, computers, groups, service accounts, shared resources, and other directory objects.
  • Maintain the domain plan, organizational-unit plan, site plan, trust plan, Group Policy design, and related architecture documentation.
  • Design and maintain an organizational-unit structure that supports administration, policy application, security boundaries, and delegated management.
  • Manage organizational-unit permissions and administrative delegation using least-privilege principles.
  • Review delegated access and correct excessive, obsolete, inherited, or conflicting permissions.
  • Develop, test, implement, maintain, and troubleshoot Group Policy Objects.
  • Manage GPO links, inheritance, precedence, security filtering, loopback processing, WMI filters, backups, version history, and recovery.
  • Evaluate proposed GPO changes for security, operational, and customer impact before production implementation.
  • Identify and resolve conflicting, obsolete, duplicative, or ineffective Group Policy settings.
  • Manage trust relationships with enterprise and external AD structures.
  • Configure, validate, monitor, and troubleshoot domain and forest trusts within approved security boundaries.
  • Review trust direction, transitivity, authentication scope, name-suffix routing, and related security settings.
  • Manage AD sites, subnets, site links, replication schedules, bridgehead behavior, and replication topology.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot replication latency, failures, lingering objects, directory inconsistencies, and site-topology problems.
  • Maintain the health of domain controllers, directory databases, SYSVOL, DFS Replication, time synchronization, and AD-integrated DNS dependencies.
  • Monitor Flexible Single Master Operations roles and support approved role transfer or seizure when necessary.
  • Plan and execute domain-controller installation, replacement, upgrade, demotion, and retirement activities.
  • Develop and implement approved plans to transition Active Directory to supported versions.
  • Manage AD schema governance and coordinate tightly controlled schema extensions.
  • Evaluate schema-change requests for compatibility, replication impact, operational risk, recovery requirements, and required approvals.
  • Maintain current directory schematics, architecture diagrams, object models, administrative boundaries, trust diagrams, and replication diagrams.
  • Administer account and group changes escalated from approved Service Desk and access-management processes.
  • Support troubleshooting of authentication, authorization, account, group-membership, policy, trust, replication, and directory-permission issues.
  • Coordinate with the Service Desk to improve identity-related ticket routing, troubleshooting, escalation, and knowledge content.
  • Provide advanced engineering support during identity, authentication, domain, and access-management incidents.
  • Identify widespread authentication failures or other outage signals and escalate them through approved incident-response procedures.
  • Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action development for recurring directory and identity incidents.
  • Develop and maintain Active Directory backup, restoration, and forest-recovery procedures.
  • Test system-state backups, directory restoration, authoritative and non-authoritative recovery, deleted-object recovery, and forest-recovery procedures.
  • Support COOP exercises, disaster-recovery testing, recovery validation, and actual continuity events.
  • Document recovery results, deficiencies, corrective actions, and lessons learned.
  • Evaluate and test approved ICAM and identity-modernization technologies.
  • Support integration testing between Active Directory and Okta or other Government-approved identity platforms.
  • Validate identity synchronization, account linking, authentication flows, group or attribute mappings, provisioning behavior, access controls, and failure handling.
  • Support testing of approved federation and modern authentication protocols such as SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth, SCIM, LDAP, or comparable technologies.
  • Coordinate identity-integration activities with cybersecurity, application owners, cloud teams, network teams, and Government identity authorities.
  • Develop test plans, test cases, expected results, rollback procedures, and validation evidence for identity integrations.
  • Evaluate modernization options while preserving required AD DS authentication, authorization, Group Policy, trust, recovery, and administrative capabilities.
  • Assess modernization proposals for interoperability, security, operational support, lifecycle, resiliency, and mission impact.
  • Automate approved directory administration, health validation, reporting, audit, and configuration activities where appropriate.
  • Review directory audit information and report activity outside approved baselines.
  • Support enforcement of DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides and approved security baselines.
  • Monitor and remediate applicable directory-service vulnerabilities, configuration findings, and policy deficiencies.
  • Support Risk Management Framework controls, assessment evidence, Plan of Action and Milestones activities, and authorization documentation.
  • Follow approved incident, problem, change, configuration, access, release, security, and quality-management processes.
  • Maintain standard operating procedures, recovery plans, configuration baselines, change records, test results, and technical documentation.
  • Provide directory-service health, availability, capacity, risk, issue, modernization, and recovery information for program reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • Minimum of eight years of relevant experience in Active Directory engineering, identity engineering, Windows infrastructure, systems engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Direct, hands-on experience engineering and administering Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services in an enterprise environment.
  • Experience managing AD objects, organizational units, Group Policy Objects, trusts, replication, schemas, delegated permissions, and directory recovery.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex authentication, authorization, Group Policy, replication, trust, and directory-services issues.
  • Experience planning or supporting Active Directory backup, restoration, disaster recovery, or forest recovery.
  • Experience testing identity integrations or evaluating enterprise identity-modernization technologies.
  • Understanding of the distinction between core AD DS administration and external ICAM, federation, or cloud-identity services.
  • Knowledge of enterprise identity security, least privilege, delegated administration, account management, and access-control principles.
  • Ability to develop and maintain architecture diagrams, domain plans, OU plans, Group Policy documentation, trust diagrams, recovery procedures, and technical standards.
  • Ability to support after-hours maintenance, COOP exercises, disaster-recovery testing, and critical incident response when required.
  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and technical problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • Experience integrating Active Directory with Okta.
  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID or hybrid identity.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense ICAM initiatives.
  • Experience with SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth, SCIM, LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, and federation technologies.
  • Experience with Active Directory Federation Services or comparable identity-provider technologies.
  • Experience with PowerShell scripting and directory-administration automation.
  • Microsoft identity, Windows Server, Azure, or security certification.
  • Okta Certified Administrator, Okta Certified Consultant, or comparable Okta certification.
  • CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or another relevant security certification.
  • Experience with CAC, PIV, certificate-based authentication, public key infrastructure, or DoD enterprise authentication.
  • Experience applying DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides to Active Directory and Windows infrastructure.
  • Experience supporting DoD Risk Management Framework controls and authorization activities.
  • Experience designing or testing identity capabilities aligned with Zero Trust principles.
  • Experience with Active Directory monitoring, privileged-access management, identity governance, or audit tools.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification.

Skills and Competencies

  • Enterprise Active Directory engineering and administration.
  • Organizational-unit and Group Policy design.
  • Trust, replication, schema, and permissions management.
  • Directory backup, restoration, and forest recovery.
  • Identity integration and modernization testing.
  • Authentication and authorization troubleshooting.
  • Security baseline and least-privilege implementation.
  • PowerShell and directory-administration automation.
  • COOP and disaster-recovery support.
  • Architecture and technical-documentation development.
  • Cross-functional identity and infrastructure coordination.
  • Strong configuration discipline and attention to detail.
  • Ability to retain deep AD DS expertise while evaluating modern ICAM capabilities.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. Should DecisionPoint Corporation. or its affiliates and teaming partners wish to initiate pre-employment discussions, you will be asked to complete an employment application and related employment documents.

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be formally employed through an Employer of Record (EOR) arrangement. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote, so you’ll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: Our client is an established Australian digital commerce consultancy that helps retailers and consumer brands build, improve, and scale their online businesses. They combine technical development, digital strategy, and customer experience expertise to deliver tailored e-commerce solutions, integrations, and ongoing platform improvements. With growing demand for online store development, they are expanding their technical capabilities to support a diverse range of projects and clients.

Role Overview: The Shopify Developer is a senior, hands-on developer who builds and ships Shopify work to a high standard, working to direction set by a Shopify Tech Lead (STL). This is a delivery role rather than a consulting one: the Developer does not own scoping, solutioning with the client, or the client relationship. They own the quality, accuracy and timeliness of what they build.

The role is expected to be deeply capable on Shopify Plus: Liquid and theme architecture, the Plus extension surfaces including Checkout UI Extensions and Customer Account Extensions, Functions, Markets, and the Storefront and Admin APIs. Hydrogen and React experience is valuable where middleware, an API proxy layer or headless components form part of a solution.

The Developer works within scope that has already been defined, but is not expected to consume a ticket passively. They estimate it honestly, interrogate it for gaps, ambiguity and hidden dependencies before starting, flag anything that looks like scope movement, and test their own work properly before it leaves their hands.

Client communication sits with the Shopify Tech Lead and the Project Manager. The Developer is not client-facing, but is expected to be an excellent communicator internally: clear written updates, early flags, and the confidence to challenge a task that does not make sense.

This role does not own: client relationships or client communication, scoping and requirements definition, solution architecture, commercial estimates issued to the client, or project coordination. Those sit with the Shopify Tech Lead, the Shopify Solution Architect and the Project Manager.

Key Responsibilities:

Development Delivery

  • Build Shopify storefront, theme, app and integration work to the agreed technical approach, meeting Amblique's coding standards and the client's acceptance criteria.
  • Work from scope and solutions defined by the Shopify Tech Lead or Solution Architect. Deliver to that design, and surface any point where it does not survive contact with implementation.
  • Deliver across BAU support, dedicated team retainers, mini projects and implementation projects, understanding that the engagement model changes the process and the tolerance for scope movement.
  • Fix defects raised in QA, UAT and post-go-live on own work within the agreed defect process, distinguishing genuine defects from change requests and raising the latter per Change Management Processes
  • Support deployment, release and go-live activity for own work, including environment checks and post-release verification.
  • Triage and resolve assigned incidents promptly, with sound judgment about severity and when to escalate.

Estimation & Scope Protection

  • Produce accurate, defensible estimates for assigned work, including allowance for testing, review and deployment, and provide them within the turnaround agreed with the Shopify Tech Lead & PM.
  • Interrogate a ticket before starting it. Where requirements are ambiguous, incomplete, or assume work that is not described, raise it before development begins rather than filling the gap silently.
  • Protect agreed scope. Where a request grows beyond what was estimated or approved, stop and flag it rather than absorbing it.
  • Flag risk to date or budget as soon as it is visible, not at the point of impact.
  • Re-estimate and communicate immediately where new information materially changes the effort required.

Quality & Developer QA

  • Test own work before it is handed on: functional testing against acceptance criteria, cross-browser and responsive checks, and regression checks on the areas touched.
  • Record evidence of developer QA on the ticket so the Shopify Tech Lead and QA can see what was covered and what was not.
  • Participate in code review, both as author and reviewer, and act on feedback rather than relitigating it.
  • Treat a defect found in own work after handover as a signal to tighten developer QA, not simply something to fix.
  • Leave the codebase in a state another developer can pick up: readable, consistent with standards, and documented where behaviour is non-obvious.

Internal Process & Communication

  • Treat Jira as the system of record. Work, decisions, blockers and time logging belong on the ticket, not in chat threads.
  • Keep tickets accurate as they move. Status and assignee updated whenever work changes hands, and priorities honoured as set, with any proposed reordering raised with the Shopify Tech Lead first.
  • Log time daily and accurately against the correct ticket.
  • Resolve confusion at the earliest point. Where direction or priority is unclear, ask in standup or directly rather than proceeding on assumption.
  • Communicate in writing, clearly and early. A blocker raised at the start of the day costs far less than the same blocker raised at the end of the week.
  • Escalate properly. If something should be solved and is not moving, raise it with the Shopify Tech Lead & PM, and escalate further if it stays stuck.
  • Handle client access and data responsibly. Use only the access granted for the account, follow the agreed environment and credential practices, and never move production customer data into local or test environments.
  • Client communication sits with the Shopify Tech Lead and the Project Manager. The Developer does not communicate directly with clients unless an alternative arrangement is agreed.

Technical Standards & AI Enablement

  • Work to the practice's coding standards, theme architecture and deployment tooling, and feed back where a standard is not working in practice.
  • Maintain awareness of Shopify platform changes, including API changes and deprecations, and flag implications for the accounts worked on.
  • Use AI tooling in development in line with the agency's AI-first direction, and contribute to improving how the team applies it.
  • Engage in internal R&D and capability-building activities during lower-workload periods.

Career Path

This is a senior individual contributor role, and the most senior development role that is not clientfacing. The pathway from here is to Shopify Tech Lead, where the engagement model allows.

Progression is based on demonstrated accuracy, the quality of delivered work, reliability of communication, and a growing ability to hold a technical conversation about a client's wider context rather than a single ticket.

Requirements

Required Skills and Qualifications:

  • 5 or more years of hands-on Shopify development, with significant time on Shopify Plus and enterprise merchant configurations.
  • Deep Liquid and theme architecture capability, including performance-conscious storefront development.
  • Hands-on experience with Shopify Plus extension surfaces, including Checkout UI Extensions and Customer Account Extensions.
  • Strong working knowledge of Shopify Functions, Markets, and the Storefront and Admin APIs.
  • Experience with custom Shopify app development, public and private.
  • Exposure to third party integration patterns such as ERP, loyalty, fulfilment and POS.
  • Hydrogen and React experience, particularly where used for middleware, an API proxy layer or headless components, is an advantage.
  • Understanding of Git workflows and CI/CD deployment pipelines in a Shopify context.
  • Proven ability to produce accurate estimates and deliver to a defined scope in an agency or professional services environment.
  • Experience with AI-assisted development tooling such as Cursor.
  • Excellent written and verbal English: able to explain technical detail clearly in writing and verbally, and to raise problems early and directly.
  • Comfortable working as part of a distributed team, with sufficient overlap with Australian Eastern business hours for daily collaboration.

Reporting Structure

  • Solid line: Shopify Practice Lead, who owns standards, tooling, workflow and team capability.
  • Day to day direction: Shopify Tech Lead on each assigned account. The Tech Lead sets the technical approach, assigns and prioritises work, and provides performance input to the Practice Lead.
  • Works closely with: Shopify Solution Architect, Shopify Tech Lead, Project Managers, Delivery Managers, other Developers, and QA.
  • Alongside the Project Manager. The Project Manager owns the commercial and delivery wrapper: scope, schedule, budget, resourcing, change control and client reporting. The Shopify Developer surfaces anything that moves date, cost or scope to the Shopify Tech Lead, who carries it to the PM and the client. Where a problem is structural or beyond the Developer's remit, the Tech Lead and PM own the client conversation.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Delivery Performance - Assigned work delivered within estimate and to agreed dates. Blockers raised the day they appear rather than at the point of impact. Incidents actioned within the agreed SLA for the account
  • Estimate Accuracy - Actual versus estimated variance under 15% on own work, excluding approved scope changes and work paused by external dependency. Estimates provided within the turnaround agreed with the Shopify Tech Lead, with testing, review and deployment effort included rather than assumed away.
  • Developer QA - Evidence of developer QA recorded on the ticket for all work, covering acceptance criteria, cross-browser and responsive checks, and regression on areas touched.
  • Technical Lead Feedback - Positive qualitative feedback from the Shopify Tech Lead and Practice Lead on code quality, reliability, responsiveness to review, and clarity of written communication.
  • Software Quality - Defects attributable to own work are found in developer QA before handover. Under 10% of defects on own work are first raised by the client during UAT or after go-live. Defects found by QA are tracked as a trend rather than a threshold, and are expected to reduce over time. No repeat defects of the same root cause. No unplanned hotfix within 48 hours of a release.
  • Scope Protection - Scope gaps, ambiguous requirements and out-of-scope requests raised before development starts, not after. Work that grows beyond what was estimated is stopped and flagged rather than absorbed
  • Jira Hygiene & Capacity Visibility - Time logged daily against the correct ticket. Status and assignee current as work moves. Capacity risk flagged at least one business day prior
  • Practice & AI Contribution - At least one meaningful internal contribution per quarter across tooling, the theme framework, R&D or AI initiatives, with time allocated by the Practice Lead rather than absorbed outside client hours.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up via an Employer of Record (EOR) service.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile

jobs.excerpt: Jeeves is the stablecoin-native banking platform for global enterprises.
jobs.description:
Jeeves is the stablecoin-native banking platform for global enterprises. Thousands of companies across 35 countries run their corporate cards, payments, treasury and spend on one platform, with more than $5B in annualized volume, payouts to 190 countries, and one of the fastest-growing stablecoin payment networks in the world. BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, Kavak and XP are among them, and more than 80% of customers use multiple Jeeves products.

We chose hard problems on purpose.

We hire for one thing: relentlessness. A strong motor that keeps going when the problem has no playbook. You'll know in your first week if Jeeves is right for you. For the right people, it's the steepest learning curve of your career.

Jeeves has raised more than $400 million in equity funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Coinbase Ventures, GIC, AllianceBernstein, CoinFund and others.

If you want to rebuild how money moves across borders, come build it with us.

Jeeves is looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our engineering team. You will design and build the backend systems that power Jeeves's financial platform — working across payments, cards, spend management, and compliance infrastructure that serves businesses across the Americas and beyond.
This is a backend engineering role at its core, we're looking for a strong backend engineer who knows how to work effectively with AI tools, understands where AI can accelerate development and product capabilities, and is comfortable integrating AI-powered features into production backend systems.
Location: This is a full-time remote position.

What You'll Do:

    Backend Engineering

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable backend services that process financial transactions and serve Jeeves customers across 20+ countries.
  • Write clean, testable, production-quality code in Go, Python, or Node.js/TypeScript; participate actively in design and code reviews.
  • Build and consume RESTful and GraphQL APIs; design inter-service communication using gRPC, message queues, and event-driven architectures.
  • Design and optimize relational and non-relational database schemas (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis) for correctness, performance, and scale.
  • Own backend features end-to-end — from scoping and technical design through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Implement security best practices: authentication, authorization, input validation, and data protection across distributed services.

    • AI-Assisted Feature Development

  • Integrate LLM API calls (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) into backend services as product features — such as spend categorization, document parsing, or natural language workflows — ensuring those integrations are reliable, observable, and cost-efficient.
  • Build backend pipelines that consume AI-generated outputs safely: validate structured outputs, handle fallback scenarios, and design graceful degradation when AI services are unavailable or return low-confidence results.
  • Collaborate with AI and data science teams to integrate model outputs into backend APIs — bridging experimental AI work and production systems.
  • Use AI coding tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude, Cursor, etc.) fluently as part of your everyday development workflow.

    • Reliability & Operations

  • Instrument services with structured logging, distributed tracing, and metrics for full operational visibility.
  • Participate in on-call rotation; respond to production incidents and contribute to post-incident reviews.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipeline improvements, testing infrastructure, and deployment practices.

    • Cross-Regional Collaboration

  • Work closely with engineering, product, compliance, and data teams across multiple time zones and regions — communicating in both English and Spanish or Portuguese as the situation requires.
  • Contribute to a globally distributed engineering culture through thorough documentation, async design reviews, and thoughtful pull request feedback.
  • Bring your regional perspective to product and engineering conversations — our LATAM customers have specific needs, and engineers who understand those markets make our product better.

Requirements:

    Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional backend engineering experience building and operating production systems.

  • Fluent in English — professional fluency required for daily work with global teams in written and spoken contexts.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one backend language: Go, Python, or Node.js/TypeScript.

  • Experience designing and building RESTful APIs, microservices, and event-driven backend systems.

jobs.description:
Tech stack:

  • Matlab, Simulink, C++17, Python, VS Code, IAR, Git, OOP paradigm, UML, Bacnet, Modbus, MP, Ethernet TCP/IP, NFC, ARM

Requirements:

  • Strong debugging and integration skills

  • Experience in Embedded SW Development (C/C++)

  • Experience with Matlab/Simulink

  • Matlab scripting (ideally OOP Matlab)

  • Modeling / Generating code

  • Hands-on experience with MCUs

  • Proactive approach to solving complex integration challenges

  • Code review experience

Nice to have:

  • Python scripting experience

Project description:

Development of various sensors and actuators within the HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) field. Examples include air differential pressure sensors, air flow sensors, ultrasonic sensors, and variable air valve actuators.

Main responsibilities:

Integration and Abstraction

  • You will integrate low-level drivers into higher-level abstractions within modular components in Simulink, following software design requirements and diagrams provided for each feature. Multiple components are then assembled into a complete feature, which is integrated into one of the many products/applications being developed within the project.

Coding and Code Generation:

  • Most of the code is written in Matlab (following OOP principles) and Simulink. C++ code generation is used to enable integration with low-level drivers written in C++.

C++ Development:

  • A custom C++ code generator has been developed for this project; part of the role involves extending and upgrading it. A strong knowledge of C++ is expected to analyze the generated code and occasionally perform direct modifications in C++.

Main Tasks of the Integrator:

  • Creating new products and integrating previously developed features. Finding and fixing bugs/defects. Creating releases and testing functionality on hardware (including specific features, communication protocols, and product parameterization/configuration).

Salary range:

  • B2B: 27 - 42 EUR/h net

  • Employment Agreement: 3.400-5.000 EURgross

jobs.title: RevOps Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About demandDrive:demandDrive is a growth-focused go-to-market agency that helps B2B organizations accelerate pipeline and revenue through integrated sales, marketing, and revenue operations solutions.
jobs.description:
About demandDrive:

demandDrive is a growth-focused go-to-market agency that helps B2B organizations accelerate pipeline and revenue through integrated sales, marketing, and revenue operations solutions. We partner with companies ranging from emerging businesses to enterprise brands to design and execute customized programs that align strategy, technology, and execution across the full customer journey. Our services include sales development, demand generation, digital marketing, website development, CRM optimization, and GTM systems support - all built to deliver measurable business outcomes. At our core, we combine smart technology, data-driven processes, and talented people to help clients grow faster and operate more efficiently.

Position Overview - RevOps Engineer:

As our RevOps Engineer, you'll own client CRM engagements end to end, from the first discovery call through blueprint, build, documentation, launch, enablement, and post-launch ROI reporting. You'll be assigned your own clients and own those relationships directly.

The split is roughly 85% client work, 15% internal. That 15% means supporting demandDrive's own HubSpot instance: executing builds and requests from our sales and marketing teams, keeping our data clean and documented, and helping use our portal as the proving ground for things we later bring to clients.

Who We're Looking For:

You know the feeling when you open a client's portal for the first time and find 340 unused properties, four lifecycle stages that all mean "kind of interested," and a pipeline where half the deals closed in 2023 and nobody noticed? Most people see a mess. You see a system that hasn't been designed yet.

We want a builder first. Someone who thinks in object models and data flows, not just workflows, and who would rather script a change from the command line than click through it one property at a time. You already work in Claude Code. You've connected it to a CRM through an MCP server, used the HubSpot CLI to build and deploy, and you have opinions about when to automate a build versus do it by hand. When something new ships, whether it's a HubSpot release, a new MCP server, or a new model, you've already tried it, watched it do something dumb, and rebuilt it with the right guardrails.

You're also business minded. Clients will hand you a list of twenty requests. You can tell which three are business critical and will actually move the needle, translate the goal behind them into clear, actionable next steps, and explain why the rest can wait.

We're an agency, so you won't be building in the background while an account manager talks to the client. You'll be in the room. You'll run discovery, write the blueprint, build it, and train the team on it. Some engagements are greenfield. Some are rescues. Some are Salesforce migrations for a team that's terrified of the change. No two CRMs look the same, and that's the fun part.

Job Responsibilities:

Client delivery (~85%)

  • Lead discovery and working sessions with stakeholders across sales, marketing, sales engineering, and post-sale delivery to document current-state process, data sources, and gaps, and translate client goals into clear, actionable next steps.
  • Separate business-critical requests from nice-to-haves, and prioritize the work that will actually move pipeline and revenue for the client.
  • Write the build blueprint covering object model, lifecycle stages, pipeline design, property architecture, automation logic, and reporting plan, then walk clients through it to sign off before configuration starts.
  • Architect and build the full CRM foundation, most often in HubSpot: property architecture, record and object customization, create forms, lifecycle and status frameworks, the Lead object, routing and assignment logic, and multi-pipeline deal processes across sales and post-sale motions.
  • Build CLI-first: use Claude Code, the HubSpot CLI, and MCP servers to script configuration, migrations, and integrations so builds are faster, version-controlled, and repeatable across clients.
  • Run data consolidation, deduplication, standardization, and migration projects, and stand up the enrichment and data quality automation that keeps the database clean after launch.
  • Design attribution models and build the dashboards and reporting infrastructure leadership actually uses to forecast, treating reporting as a design input from day one rather than a final step.
  • Build with AI where it earns its place: Claude Code and MCP-connected agents working against live CRM data, plus HubSpot's Breeze agents, Agent Builder, and Breeze Assistant, with the governance and guardrails to match.
  • Deliver enablement including recorded training, written documentation, admin enablement for the client's internal system owner, and post-launch support through the first weeks of real usage.
  • Build and maintain documentation of each client’s HubSpot instance, covering object model, properties, automation logic, and integrations, so the system stays understandable long after launch.
  • Track and report on post-launch ROI, tying what was built back to the business goals set in discovery.
  • Scope change orders and retainer expansions honestly, and tell clients when they should wait on something rather than buy it.

Internal HubSpot support (~15%)

  • Provide support for demandDrive's HubSpot instance by executing internal builds and projects that align with the defined strategy.
  • Execute requests from internal teams, from quick fixes to real builds.
  • Keep our own data, reporting, and automation in the shape we'd want a client's to be in.
  • Build and maintain documentation of our instance so configuration, automation, and changes are tracked.
  • Pilot new HubSpot releases, MCP servers, and AI tooling internally so we know what's real before we recommend it.

Job Requirements & Qualifications:

  • CRM Experience (HubSpot Is Non-Negotiable) You need deep, hands-on HubSpot expertise across Sales Hub and Marketing Hub at minimum, ideally Service and Content too. Custom objects and association labels. Lifecycle stage architecture. The Lead object and lead pipelines. Multi-pipeline deal processes with stage gating and required properties. Workflow automation at real complexity. Permissions, teams, and portal governance. Custom report builder and dashboards. You know where the platform's edges are and you design inside them instead of promising around them. Hands-on Attio or Salesforce experience is a plus.
  • Builder Mindset: Claude Code, CLIs & MCPs You build with Claude Code day to day, not just as a chat window. You've used CLIs, including the HubSpot CLI, to build and deploy, and you've set up or built MCP servers that connect Claude to a CRM. You reach for the command line when it's faster and more repeatable than clicking, you keep your work in version control, and you review what an agent produced before it touches a client's live data.
  • Data Hub, Enrichment & Data Quality Working knowledge of HubSpot Data Hub: data sync, data quality automation, formatting rules, property validation, datasets, and where credits get consumed. You understand HubSpot's native enrichment across automatic, continuous, and manual modes, what it can and can't fill in, and how to set realistic expectations on match rates. You've run a real deduplication and cleanup project and know when native tooling is enough versus when a third-party tool needs to come in.
  • AI-First Thinking, Including Agent Builder You approach every problem by asking where AI does the heavy lifting. You're familiar with HubSpot's Agent Hub and Agent Builder, building custom agents and agentic workflows on live CRM data, wiring triggers, configuring knowledge sources, and testing before publishing. You think about credit consumption, run limits, and human review on consequential actions, because agents that write to the CRM without guardrails create cleanup work instead of removing it. You're also comfortable building with Claude and other leading models outside of HubSpot, and you stay current as the landscape moves.
  • Client Leadership & Business Judgment You can run a discovery session with a VP of Sales and a skeptical sales engineer in the same room, ask the questions that surface the real process, scope a solution, and communicate clearly about what you're building and when it lands. You can say "that's out of scope, here's what it would take" without it becoming a problem. You translate client goals into clear, actionable next steps, and you can tell which requests are business critical and will actually move the needle versus which ones just feel urgent. You don't need hand-holding in client situations.
  • Reporting & Attribution You've built forecasting, closed-won, and operational accountability reporting that leadership trusts. You understand attribution models, first touch versus latest touch and why most clients don't need multi-touch, and how to enforce data capture so the reports hold up.
  • Technical Foundation Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, and the command line. You can build an integration or debug a sync issue without pulling in a developer. Light scripting in Python or JavaScript is a plus, as are custom coded actions in HubSpot workflows.
  • Data Migration You've moved real data into HubSpot from spreadsheets, another CRM, or somewhere worse. You know how to build import templates, handle associations, backfill historical records, and set expectations about what won't survive the trip.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience at a HubSpot Solutions Partner or RevOps consulting firm.
  • HubSpot certifications, especially Architecture, Data Integrations, or Solutions Partner-level credentials.
  • Attio or Salesforce experience, particularly migrations to or from HubSpot.
  • Experience building your own MCP servers, Claude Code skills, or HubSpot developer projects.
  • Automation tools like Zapier, n8n, or Make for connecting systems HubSpot doesn't natively reach.
  • Familiarity with compliance-adjacent constraints like SOC 2, CMMC, and HIPAA, and how they shape what belongs in a CRM.
  • Active in HubSpot or RevOps communities.

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Salary: $80,000 to $90,000, depending on experience.
  • Schedule: M-F, 9am-5pm - hybrid or remote work model (must reside in the U.S.).
  • Structure: Full-time, reporting to the Sr. RevOps Manager.
  • Health coverage and other health & wellness benefits via BCBS, vision care, dental coverage (Delta Dental), paid paternity & maternity leave, life & disability insurance, 401(k) matching.
  • Paid time-off and 14 paid holidays.
  • Positive team culture.
  • Company laptop, full tech stack, tools, and other resources provided by demandDrive.
